source_title: Choosing Diagnostic Labs, Cheap Packages & Predictive Tests - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
At the Healthtech Summit, diagnostic experts and medical leaders examined criteria for selecting pathology laboratories and utilizing modern diagnostic tools. The panel addressed risks associated with commercial testing packages and misleading marketing, urging patients to prioritize laboratory accreditation, physician supervision, quality control, and clinical history. Panellists evaluated screenings for lifestyle diseases including diabetes and cardiovascular conditions, while addressing the clinical impacts of over-testing and missed diagnoses. The summit also explored predictive medicine, whole-body imaging, gut microbiome profiling, genetic sequencing, and coronary calcium scoring for disease risk stratification. Medical practitioners emphasized the requirement for clinical guidance and pre-test counselling for advanced procedures. Addressing antimicrobial resistance, the panel called for replacing outdated diagnostics, such as the Widal test for typhoid, with targeted methodologies to reduce unnecessary antibiotic prescriptions. Additionally, the discussions covered the application of artificial intelligence in radiology and pathology, outlining how clinical algorithms serve as precision decision-support tools alongside specialist physicians. PM Launches Banaskantha Projects, Slams Opposition Over 'Fake Narrative'
During his visit to Banaskantha, Gujarat, the Prime Minister launched development projects worth around 14,400 crore rupees and is scheduled to announce 19,000 crore rupees under the PM-Kisan scheme. Addressing the public, he made scathing remarks against opposition parties, accusing them of spreading fake narratives and attempting to cause anarchy amid calls demanding his resignation. The Prime Minister highlighted his government's handling of global supply disruptions, specifically addressing issues related to gas and urea availability for women and farmers, and asserted his commitment to serving the public till his last breath.
PM Kisan Instalment Released; Dairy Projects and Metro Expansion Unveiled in Gujarat
During a public address in Banaskantha, Gujarat, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the disbursement of the latest instalment of the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi, transferring over 18,000 crore rupees to around 10 crore farmers across India. He highlighted that government initiatives such as subsidized fertilizers, MSP procurement, PM Fasal Bima Yojana, and the PM KUSUM solar scheme have cumulatively benefited farmers with over 50 lakh crore rupees in savings and transfers. The Prime Minister underscored technological advancements in agriculture and animal husbandry, citing the distribution of over 26 crore Soil Health Cards, breed conservation via IVF, and nationwide cattle vaccination drives. He also dedicated and laid the foundation stones for key infrastructure projects, including two new train services, the Ahmedabad Metro extension to GIFT City and the airport, highway widening, cluster development programmes for horticulture, and modern Anganwadis across Gujarat, while inviting citizens to join the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations.
UP's 1090 Women Powerline: Tackling Harassment, FFR Method, & 30-Day Follow-Up
In Uttar Pradesh, the Women Powerline 1090 serves as a crucial support channel for women facing harassment over phone calls or social media. Upon receiving a complaint, police initiate action by issuing a warning call directly to the accused. If the misconduct persists, authorities employ the Family, Friends, and Relatives technique to contact close associates of the offender. Operating through a 150-seat call centre handling approximately 8,000 incoming and 10,000 outgoing calls daily, the helpline also offers emotional support and counselling to complainants. To guarantee long-term safety, police conduct a follow-up 30 days after action is taken, reopening the resolution process if harassment continues.
PM Modi Slams Opposition in Banaskantha Over Anarchy, Launches Rs 14,400-Crore Projects
Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched development projects worth approximately 14,400 crore rupees in Banaskantha, Gujarat, reflecting on his 25-year political journey from the state. In his address, he launched a sharp attack against the opposition, accusing them of spreading fake narratives about shortages of gas and urea amid global supply disruptions caused by the US-Iran conflict. He stated that these narratives were designed to gain control and spread anarchy across the country. Modi affirmed that the government ensured uninterrupted urea supplies at existing rates and resolved to serve the public until his last breath, with plans to announce an additional 19,000 crore rupees under the PM-Kisan scheme.
